title: What is monitored containment?
question: What is monitored containment?
answer: Monitored containment means a model is exercised under observation so that any attempt to overstep its boundary — an escape, an egress, an unsanctioned action — is seen and recorded rather than silently possible. It is a measured, observed regime, not a claim of provable isolation. We say this precisely: monitored containment, not provable isolation. The distinction matters the same way the 2026-08-04 AISI finding did — access that is config-GIVEN and watched is different from access that is taken.
ref: Council of AI containment series, v0.1 incident index (2026-08-13 build)
